### Building a New Desktop PC – A Step‑by‑Step Guide Below you’ll find everything from choosing parts to installing your first operating system. Whether you’re building a gaming rig, an editing workstation, or a simple home computer, this checklist will keep you organized and help avoid common pitfalls. --- #### 1️⃣ Define Your Purpose & Budget | Use Case | Typical Specs | Rough Price Range | |----------|---------------|-------------------| | **Gaming** | GPU: RTX 3060/3070+
CPU: Ryzen 5/7 or Intel i5/i7
M.2 NVMe SSD + 500GB–1TB | $800–$2000 | | **Content Creation / Video Editing** | CPU: Ryzen 9 / Intel i9
GPU: RTX 3080/4090 or AMD Radeon RX 6800 XT
RAM: ≥32 GiB | $1500–$3000 | | **Office / Everyday Use** | CPU: Core i3/Ryzen 3
Integrated graphics or entry‑level discrete card
SSD: 256–512 GB | <$400 | *Tip:* Start with a rough total cost estimate; then use sites like [PCPartPicker](https://pcpartpicker.com/) to see how far you get within that range. --- #### 2️⃣ Gather Components | Component | What to Look For | Why It Matters | |-----------|------------------|----------------| | **Case** | Size (ATX/Micro‑ATX/LGA1200 etc.), airflow, cable routing space | Determines what motherboards & GPUs fit | | **Motherboard** | Socket type (AM4, LGA1151, LGA1700...), chipset features, form factor, expansion slots | Must match CPU socket & case size | | **Processor (CPU)** | Performance tier, integrated vs dedicated GPU, power draw (TDP) | Drives overall performance | | **Memory (RAM)** | Capacity (8–64 GiB), speed (DDR4/DDR5), dual‑channel support | Faster RAM improves multitasking & games | | **Storage** | M.2 NVMe SSD (fast boot), SATA HDD if extra bulk storage | Fast storage speeds up load times | | **Graphics Card (GPU)** | VRAM amount, output ports, cooling solution | Essential for gaming/video work | | **Power Supply Unit (PSU)** | Wattage (adequate headroom), modular cables, efficiency rating (80 Plus Bronze/Silver/Gold) | Supplies stable power | | **Cooling System** | Stock cooler vs aftermarket air/liquid cooler | Keeps temperatures low under load | | **Operating System** | Windows 10/11, Linux distro, license key | Needed after hardware install | | **Peripherals** | Monitor, keyboard, mouse, speakers/headset | Not part of internal build but essential for testing | *(Optional)* **Additional accessories:** thermal paste (if not pre-applied), anti-static wrist strap, screwdrivers, zip ties, cable combs. --- #### 3️⃣ Prepare Workspace 1. **Clean area** – flat surface free of static electricity. 2. **Anti‑static mat** or wear an antistatic wristband. 3. **Organize screws** – group them by component so nothing gets lost. 4. **Keep manuals handy** – motherboard manual often contains mounting diagrams. --- #### 4️⃣ Install the Power Supply First 1. Place PSU into its bay at bottom/back of the case. 2. Secure it with two screws. 3. Route main 24‑pin ATX connector toward the motherboard. 4. Connect the 12V EPS connector (usually 4‑or‑8‑pin). 5. Keep spare cables accessible for later stages. --- #### 5️⃣ Mount the Motherboard 1. Align standoffs inside the case with holes on the board. *If using a non‑standard layout, double‑check spacing.* 2. Screw the motherboard onto the standoffs lightly—don’t overtighten yet. 3. Attach I/O shield plate to rear panel before fully securing the board. --- #### 6️⃣ Insert the Processor 1. Lift the CPU socket lever. 2. Line up the triangle marker on the processor with the one on the socket. 3. Gently place the CPU down; do NOT force it. 4. Lower the lever to lock the CPU in place. --- #### 7️⃣ Apply Thermal Paste & Install Cooler - If your cooler comes with pre‑applied paste, skip step 1. - Otherwise apply a pea‑size dot of high‑quality thermal paste (e.g., Arctic MX‑Pro). - Mount the cooler according to manufacturer’s instructions. - Connect fan header(s) to the appropriate headers on the motherboard. --- #### 8️⃣ Install Memory (RAM) 1. Unlock DIMM slot latch(es). 2. Snap RAM sticks firmly into place until latches click back. 3. Verify correct orientation via notch alignment. --- #### 9️⃣ Add Storage Devices - **NVMe SSD**: Slide into M.2 slot, secure with small screw. - **SATA drives/HDDs**: Mount into drive bays, connect data cable to motherboard and power cable to PSU. --- #### 🔟 Fit the Graphics Card 1. Remove necessary PCI‑Express riser or expansion slot covers on the case. 2. Insert GPU into topmost PCI‑E x16 slot; push gently until seated. 3. Lock the bracket with a screw. 4. Connect required PCI‑E power connectors from PSU to GPU. --- ##### ⚡️ Final Cable Management Tips - Bundle excess cables together with zip ties. - Run long cables through designated grommets or cutouts. - Leave enough slack for future upgrades or cleaning. --- #### 🧩 Plug Everything In 1. **Front Panel Connections** – USB, audio jacks, power button, reset switch. 2. **Back Panel Cables** – HDMI/DVI/VGA from GPU, front‑panel LEDs, fans. 3. **Check all connections** – ensure none are loose. --- #### 📦 Close Up & Test 1. Double‑check all screws and cable routes. 2. Replace side panels. 3. Turn on the system once. 4. Enter BIOS/UEFI immediately (often `Del` or `F2`). In BIOS: - Confirm CPU, memory, and storage are detected correctly. - Set boot priority to your primary storage device. - Enable XMP profile for DDR4/DDR5 RAM (recommended). Press “Save & Exit” → system should reboot. --- #### 🎉 Operating System Installation 1. Create a bootable USB stick with your chosen OS installer (`Rufus`, `balenaEtcher`). 2. Boot from USB → follow prompts to format target disk and install OS. 3. Once installed, update drivers: - **Windows**: Device Manager → Update driver → Search automatically. - **Linux**: Most distributions auto-detect drivers; run package manager updates. Install core utilities (web browser, office suite, antivirus as desired). --- #### 🚀 Post‑Build Checklist | Item | Action | |------|--------| | **Thermal Monitoring** | Check temps during idle/load (HWMonitor, MSI Afterburner). | | **Fan Speeds** | Adjust PWM curves in BIOS or software. | | **BIOS Updates** | Download latest firmware from motherboard vendor. | | **Cable Cleanliness** | Reorganise if airflow feels restricted. | | **Backup Plan** | Consider external backup or cloud sync. | --- ### Common Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them | Issue | Prevention Tip | |-------|----------------| | **Short circuits** | Always unplug PSU when working internally. | | **Overheating** | Ensure adequate ventilation; consider additional case fans. | | **Component incompatibility** | Cross‑reference specs on PCPartPicker; check compatibility lists. | | **Missing screws** | Store screws separately per component; label containers. | | **Boot failure** | Verify BIOS settings; re-seat problematic modules. | --- ### Resources for Visual Guidance - **YouTube Channels**: Linus Tech Tips, JayzTwoCents, Paul's Hardware. - **Forums**: r/buildapc (Reddit), Tom's Hardware Build Guides. - **Software**: PCPartPicker for budgeting & compatibility checks. Happy building! Feel free to drop me a question if you hit snags along the way.
